One possibility worth examining is that your experience of helping your friend move was connected to a sense of being needed. This might be tied to a reflex to guard what it loves, which is a quality that shows up in your Baseline. When you help someone, especially a close friend, it could be that this creates a temporary sense of value or importance. This, in turn, might be influencing your mood and behavior since the move, making you feel heavy and quiet.

It may be worth looking at whether being needed has become connected to feeling valuable. If that connection is present, it could make certain relationships feel especially important even when they are costly to you. What does helping mean to you? Does it mean being needed, or is there another aspect to it? 

What keeps happening in this situation? You've been feeling heavy and quiet since helping your friend, and this has carried over to your work. One way to see this is as a dynamic where your sense of value and importance is tied to being needed, and when that's not happening, you feel off.
